entries.title: Midnight Deploy
entries.feel: I felt completely hollowed out, feeling the weight of the upcoming project deadline.
entries.event: Pushed an emergency hotfix at 1am after a sprint deploy incident that was partly my fault.
entries.action: Wrote an honest post-mortem, sent it on Slack, and closed the laptop.

entries.title: Invisible in the Standup
entries.feel: That specific tiredness of being talked over — and Slack alerts ringing in my ears.
entries.event: Raised an architectural concern in the sprint standup before the deadline. Same senior engineer interrupted me.
entries.action: Sent a Slack message to my manager with a Notion link. Not sure she read it.

entries.title: The Quarter Review
entries.feel: Pride mixed with something defensive — like I had to justify being good at my job.
entries.event: Performance review. Got 'meets expectations' despite shipping three major features solo.
entries.action: Scheduled a 1:1 to ask what 'exceeds' actually looks like. Determined to get a real answer this time.

entries.title: Eight Hours of Flow
entries.feel: Rare and almost euphoric — the kind of focus you can't manufacture.
entries.event: Solved the concurrency bug blocking the team for the sprint.
entries.action: Muted Slack notifications to focus, documented the fix, and left at 5pm.

entries.title: Deadline Again
entries.feel: Numb. I've stopped feeling the urgency and that worries me more than the urgency itself.
entries.event: Third sprint in a row where scope expanded on the last day before the deadline.
entries.action: Blocked two hours tomorrow morning — no Slack, no meetings — just to think about whether this is sustainable.

entries.title: Shipped It
entries.feel: Quiet satisfaction, the kind that doesn't need an audience.
entries.event: Feature went live with zero bugs reported in the first 24 hours.
entries.action: Told no one at work. Went home and cooked a proper dinner for the first time in two weeks.

entries.title: The Exit Interview Thought
entries.feel: Scared of how calm I felt imagining leaving.
entries.event: A recruiter reached out on LinkedIn. I didn't delete the message.
entries.action: Wrote out a list of what I'd need to stay. Kept it to myself for now.

entries.title: First Run in the Rain
entries.feel: Uncomfortable at first then something opened up — like I was finally outside my own head.
entries.event: Set out at 6am despite the weather. Ran 5k. Didn't stop once.
entries.action: Left my shoes by the door so I'd have no excuse tomorrow.

entries.title: The Wall
entries.feel: My legs felt like wet concrete and I genuinely hated every person I saw enjoying themselves.
entries.event: Attempted a 10k. Hit the wall at 7km. Walked the rest.
entries.action: Ate a banana, realized I should have done yoga instead of over-running.

entries.title: Yoga Breakthrough
entries.feel: Something physical released in my chest that I didn't know was held.
entries.event: Pigeon pose. I've been avoiding it for months. Today I stayed in it for two minutes.
entries.action: Booked three more yoga classes for this month.

entries.title: Knee Scare
entries.feel: That specific fear of the body betraying you before you've finished with it.
entries.event: Sharp pain in my left knee mid-run. Stopped immediately.
entries.action: Iced it, booked a physio appointment, and decided to stick to gentle yoga.

entries.title: Personal Best
entries.feel: Disbelief first, then a kind of animal joy.
entries.event: 5k in 22:14. Two months ago I couldn't run a kilometre without stopping.
entries.action: Texted my brother. He said 'that's genuinely impressive' and I believed him.

entries.title: Rest Day Guilt
entries.feel: Missed my morning yoga session and felt irrational guilt for resting.
entries.event: Took a full rest day. Didn't run, didn't stretch, didn't do anything athletic.
entries.action: Wrote out what recovery actually does physiologically. Read it twice.

entries.title: The Conversation About Distance
entries.feel: Braced the whole time, like waiting for something to break.
entries.event: Talked with my partner about being less present lately. Neither of us blamed the other.
entries.action: Suggested we have dinner without phones on Thursday. She said yes.

entries.title: Thursday Dinner
entries.feel: Reminded me why I chose this person. It was that simple.
entries.event: Cooked dinner and talked for three hours with my partner. No phones. No agenda.
entries.action: Told her I'd been scared she was pulling away. She said she'd felt the same about me.

entries.title: She Cried and I Froze
entries.feel: A cold wave of helplessness. I wanted to fix it and knew I couldn't.
entries.event: My partner got difficult news about her mother. We talked but I froze.
entries.action: I said 'I don't know what to say but I'm here.' She leaned into me. That was enough.

entries.title: Laughing Until We Couldn't
entries.feel: Weightless. Like nothing difficult had happened or would happen.
entries.event: My partner and I watched old home videos and laughed until we cried.
entries.action: Saved the best one to rewatch when things feel heavy.

entries.title: Different Futures
entries.feel: A kind of quiet dread I've been pretending isn't there.
entries.event: My partner mentioned moving cities in two years. Need to actually talk about it.
entries.action: Didn't react in the moment. Wrote this instead.

entries.title: How She Sees Me
entries.feel: Something between gratitude and discomfort — like I'd been caught being more than I pretend to be.
entries.event: She described me to her friend on the phone without knowing I could hear. She said I was thoughtful and that I notice things.
entries.action: Told her later that I'd heard. She didn't seem embarrassed at all.

entries.title: The Anniversary Fight
entries.feel: That specific shame of knowing I'm wrong mid-argument and continuing anyway.
entries.event: We argued on our anniversary about something that had nothing to do with the real issue.
entries.action: Apologised properly the next morning. Told her the real issue. She had been waiting for me to say it.

entries.title: The Canvas I Couldn't Finish
entries.feel: Frustration that felt like it was about the painting but was really about everything else.
entries.event: Worked on the large canvas for three hours. Painted over the whole thing at the end.
entries.action: Left it white. Decided the white canvas is finished. Put it on the wall.

entries.title: Song at 2am
entries.feel: That strange combination of being drained and completely alive.
entries.event: Finished writing a song I'd been stuck on for weeks. The bridge came out of nowhere.
entries.action: Recorded a rough voice memo. Resisted the urge to perfect it immediately.

entries.title: Showing the Work
entries.feel: Naked. Genuinely unsure if I'd made something real or something I'd just told myself was real.
entries.event: Showed my sketchbook to a friend who's a proper artist. She turned each page slowly.
entries.action: She said 'you have a specific eye.' I wrote that down exactly.

entries.title: Nothing for Weeks
entries.feel: That specific creative paralysis that feels like emptiness but is really too full.
entries.event: Hadn't made anything in three weeks. Kept opening notebooks and closing them.
entries.action: Bought new pencils. Sometimes the ritual is enough to start.

entries.title: Someone Else Painted My Idea
entries.feel: Irrational irritation followed by something harder to name — maybe the grief of a path not taken.
entries.event: Saw a painting at a gallery that was almost exactly the concept I'd had in my head for months.
entries.action: Bought a small print of it. Put it above my desk. Made peace with it.

entries.title: Mum Called Twice
entries.feel: Guilt with a texture — not sharp, more like something wearing down.
entries.event: Missed her calls on Tuesday. Called back Thursday. She said it was fine. It wasn't fine.
entries.action: Set a recurring Sunday call in my calendar. Not negotiable.

entries.title: Dad's Advice
entries.feel: An unexpected softness — the kind that only comes from being known a long time.
entries.event: Told my dad about the work situation. He listened for twenty minutes without interrupting.
entries.action: He said 'you've always figured it out.' I didn't argue. That was new.

entries.title: The Old Argument
entries.feel: The exhaustion of a pattern you can see coming and still can't stop.
entries.event: Family dinner with my older brother. Same dynamic as always — my brother talks, I retreat, Mum mediates.
entries.action: Left early. Texted my sister about it. She said she'd noticed it for years.

entries.title: Hometown for the Weekend
entries.feel: Nostalgia as a physical sensation — warm and slightly suffocating.
entries.event: Visited my parents and my older brother in my hometown for the first time in four months.
entries.action: Told my mum she looked well. She lit up. I should say things like that more often.

entries.title: My Brother's News
entries.feel: Genuine joy followed by an honest flicker of envy I'm not proud of.
entries.event: My brother announced his engagement. Everyone cried. It was a good moment.
entries.action: Called my brother separately to congratulate him properly, without an audience.

entries.title: A Good Walk
entries.feel: Simple and uncomplicated. That's worth writing down.
entries.event: Walked for an hour with no destination. Listened to one album all the way through.
entries.action: Nothing. That was the point.

entries.title: The 3am Thought
entries.feel: That specific 3am clarity that will be completely gone by morning.
entries.event: Couldn't sleep. Started thinking about what I actually want my life to look like in five years.
entries.action: Wrote three lines. Read them at 9am. Still meant something.

entries.title: Overheard Kindness
entries.feel: An unexpected warmth, like finding something you forgot you'd lost.
entries.event: On the bus, a teenager gave up their seat without being asked. Nobody acknowledged it.
entries.action: Smiled at them when they sat down near me. They looked confused. I didn't explain.

entries.title: The Book I Couldn't Finish
entries.feel: Something between boredom and responsibility — like I owed it to the author.
entries.event: Tried for the third time to finish a novel I bought eight months ago. Got to page 200. Stopped.
entries.action: Put it in the charity bag. Let it go.

entries.title: Wrong Coffee Order
entries.feel: An outsized irritation that I knew, even then, was not about the coffee.
entries.event: Got the wrong order at the café. Didn't say anything. Sat with it.
entries.action: Tried to figure out what I was actually upset about. Still not sure.

entries.title: Deadlines Feel Different Now
entries.feel: The same pressure as before, but now it feels like it's happening to someone else.
entries.event: Three sprint deadlines this week. I handled them all. I'm not sure that's a good sign.
entries.action: Booked a day off next week. Something I've never done mid-sprint before.

entries.title: Running in the Dark
entries.feel: Slightly afraid, mostly alive. The city is a different place at 5am.
entries.event: Alarm failed, went out at 5am instead of 6 for a run. The streets were empty.
entries.action: Decided 5am is better. Set the alarm for 5 tomorrow.

entries.title: Missing Her When She's There
entries.feel: A pre-emptive grief that doesn't make sense but also makes complete sense.
entries.event: We were in the same room reading. I looked up and felt sad that this moment would end.
entries.action: Told her. She put down her book and looked at me for a long time.

entries.title: Drawing from Memory
entries.feel: Strangely intimate — like accessing a part of myself I'd been ignoring.
entries.event: Drew my grandmother from memory. No reference. Spent two hours on it.
entries.action: Photographed it and sent it to my mum. She called immediately.

entries.title: Sibling Silence Broken
entries.feel: Tentative hope, like testing ice you're not sure will hold.
entries.event: My sister and brother texted out of nowhere after three months of no contact. Just 'how are you?'
entries.action: Replied honestly. Said it had been hard. She said 'me too.' We talked for an hour.
